cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Mathematical modelling predicts performance before manufacture, saving time and cost in development.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Stress = Force / Area (units: N/mm2 or MPa); always identify the cross-sectional area carrying the load.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Strain = Change in length / Original length (dimensionless ratio or percentage).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Young's Modulus (E) = Stress / Strain (units: GPa); measures stiffness of a material — higher E means stiffer.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Density = Mass / Volume (units: kg/m3); used to calculate component weight from its volume.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Factor of Safety = Ultimate tensile strength / Working stress; accounts for uncertainties in loading and material properties.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: CAD simulation (FEA — Finite Element Analysis) models stress distribution in complex components visually.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Calculations for area, volume and mass are needed to predict weight and material costs: volume of a cylinder = pi x r2 x h.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Resistors in series: Rtotal = R1 + R2 + R3; in parallel: 1/Rtotal = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Force, weight and mass: Weight = mass x g (where g = 9.81 m/s2); always distinguish mass (kg) from weight (N).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: Scaling models: a model at 1/10 scale has 1/1000 of the volume and mass of the full-size product.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Modelling & Calculation
cards.back: CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) models airflow around products to optimise aerodynamic performance.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — modelling & calculation?
cards.back: 1. For Modelling & Calculation questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Modelling & Calculation through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant

An engineer is designing a steel lifting eye that must support a load of 50 kN with a factor of safety of 5. The steel has a UTS of 600 MPa. Calculate the minimum cross-sectional area required and determine a suitable rod diameter. [6 marks]
